text:
Frank Nazar might be the best thing happening in Chicago right now. He has 11 goals in 21 games, eight of them in his last ten, a five-game point streak, and his ice time is up more than a minute and a half a night over that stretch. With Connor Bedard hurt again, the Blackhawks are leaning on him.

How much of it is real? Partly. His chances are up a little (3.7 expected goals on his own shots over ten games against 3.3 usual), and the Moore-Nazar-Kane line ranks among the better lines in the league by shot share, per The Athletic's Scott Powers. But 11 goals on 6.9 expected means a 24% shooting rate after 11% last season. That will come down.

There is a counterweight: Chicago has scored 6.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him assists (he has only three). He also has the tools, with 90th percentile top speed and shot velocity by NHL Edge tracking. Our range has him at 23 to 37 goals for the season.
